title: Agent
description: An immutable, content-addressed agent definition (ADR-0022 §1). An Agent is declarative data, never code. Editing one produces a new version rather than mutating the existing definition, because a run pins a version for its entire life and an in-place edit would silently change the behaviour of work already in flight. The definition deliberately omits the objective and the output schema: those are per-node, live in the Graph, and are already pinned by graphVersionHash (ADR-0022 §2). An agent is reusable behaviour; a node is one specific use of it.

schemaVersion.description: ADR-0024 §5: stored documents are versioned as data. One version exists in V1.

agentId.description: Names the agent, not the definition. Stable across versions; this is what a Graph references.

agentVersionHash.description: Names the exact definition: sha256 of its canonical form per ADR-0020. Excluded from the canonical form before hashing, since a document cannot contain its own hash. Assigned at publication, not by the author.

systemInstructions.description: Platform-authored instruction blocks. ADR-0004 §8: untrusted content — repository files, issue text, page bodies, pull-request comments — must never appear here. It belongs in the ContextBundle, where it is marked UNTRUSTED and rendered where the protocol expects data rather than instructions.

defaultModelPolicy.description: The agent's default model. A node may override it. Expressed as either a capability selector or a concrete pinned reference; the selector form exists so an agent definition need not be re-published when a provider retires a model version.

modelRef.description: A logical name resolved by the model gateway, not a provider model id (ADR-0010 §1). Callers never name a provider model directly.

defaultBudgets.description: Defaults for the agent loop. maxIterations bounds the agent's internal reason-act loop within one node attempt — it is not the graph loop bound of ADR-0021 §4, which is a property of a loop node.

capabilityCeiling.description: The most this agent may ever be granted, extending the derivation chain of ADR-0014 §5: platform policy contains trust-level ceiling contains registry record contains agent ceiling contains node request. Monotonically non-increasing at every step. Its value is that a general-purpose agent can be denied IRREVERSIBLE tools once, centrally, instead of in every node that uses it. Validated against platform policy at publication (ADR-0022 §6), so an over-broad agent cannot be published and then discovered in production.

outputContractStyle.description: STRUCTURED: the agent is expected to produce output validating against the node's declared output schema. FREEFORM: prose, permissible only where no downstream transition depends on the shape.
